subtitle: The bridge between analog and digital worlds. Audio interfaces convert your instrument and microphone signals into digital audio your computer can record and process.

introduction.title: What is an Audio Interface?
introduction.text: An audio interface is a hardware device that connects your instruments, microphones, and studio monitors to your computer. It handles analog-to-digital conversion (ADC) for recording and digital-to-analog conversion (DAC) for playback.

columns.title: Key Functions
columns.text: Convert analog signals to digital (ADC). Convert digital signals to analog (DAC). Provide phantom power for condensers. Offer low-latency monitoring. Supply multiple inputs/outputs. Improve audio quality over built-in cards.

columns.title: Why You Need One
columns.text: Better sound quality than computer audio. Professional XLR and TRS connections. Multiple simultaneous recordings. Direct monitoring without delay. Dedicated preamps for microphones. Proper impedance matching.

fields.label: Latency
fields.value: Round-trip under 10ms ideal for real-time monitoring

cards.title: High Latency
cards.description: Lower buffer size in DAW settings, use ASIO drivers, close background apps, upgrade to faster interface.

cards.title: No Signal/Crackling Audio
cards.description: Check connections, update drivers, try different USB port, adjust sample rate, check phantom power settings.

cards.title: Interface Not Recognized
cards.description: Install manufacturer drivers, try different cable/port, check device manager, restart computer and interface.
